# Review of FDS Section 6.2: Tank Pressure Control

## Defect List

| # | Clause | Severity | Defect | Required correction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | 6.2.3 | **Critical** | The high-high tank pressure trip stops the BOG compressors. This removes the main means of pressure relief when pressure is already high, so the tank is driven toward its PSVs. The stated purpose ("to protect them") is wrong. Tank HH is a tank-protection function, and compressor protection belongs on the compressor's own instruments. | Redefine PAHH as a tank-protection SIF. It should stop vapour and heat inputs (filling, unloading, recirculation), force the flare valve fully open and keep the compressors running. Compressor protection goes on compressor package instrumentation. |
| D2 | 6.2.4 | **Critical** | Operators can bypass a safety trip from the HMI with no controls. This is not compliant with IEC 61511 bypass management, and it is not appropriate for an operator-accessible HMI function. | Bypasses only through a key or permit-controlled maintenance override, logged and time-limited. A persistent alarm must show while bypassed. Compensating measures must be defined. No bypass during filling or unloading. Sensor-level bypass only, so voting degrades rather than defeats the function. |
| D3 | 6.2.5 | **Critical** | Claims that tank low pressure is "not a concern". Vacuum or low pressure is a credible hazard. Causes include compressor overdraw, barometric pressure rise, liquid send-out or pump-out, cold or subcooled LNG filling (vapour collapse) and the flare valve failing open. Air ingress through vacuum relief creates a flammable atmosphere in the tank. | Add low-pressure alarm, low-pressure override on compressor capacity, PALL trip, and a makeup or vacuum-breaker gas supply ahead of the vacuum relief valves. |
| D4 | 6.2.5 | Major | "Compressors run continuously" ignores real operating cases. These include turndown below minimum compressor capacity, duty/standby operation, loss of the BOG outlet (recondenser, send-out or fuel gas unavailable), and high-BOG cases such as ship unloading, cooldown or rollover. | Define the operating modes, duty/standby, minimum-flow handling and the response to loss of BOG outlet. |
| D5 | 6.2.2 | Major | Tag mismatch: PIC-510 is said to operate PV-512. | Align controller and valve loop numbers with the P&ID (e.g. PIC-512 / PV-512) and confirm. |
| D6 | 6.2.2 | Major | Flare control is described only on rising pressure. There is no close-on-low-pressure override, so a stuck-open or slow-closing flare valve can draw the tank toward vacuum. Fail position, controller action and independence from PIC-501 are not stated. | Specify setpoint, action, fail position (per HAZOP), a low-pressure close override, and that it uses a transmitter separate from PIC-501. |
| D7 | 6.2 general | Major | No stated tank design pressure or design vacuum. The setpoint hierarchy cannot be verified, and margins for valve stroke time, transmitter accuracy and accumulation are not shown. | State design pressure and vacuum from the tank vendor. Tabulate the full pressure hierarchy. |
| D8 | 6.2.3 | Major | SIF not defined: no transmitters, no voting, no independence from the control system, no SIL, no actions, no reset philosophy. | Reference the SRS. Use dedicated SIS transmitters (e.g. 2oo3), SIL from LOPA, and manual reset only. |
| D9 | 6.2 general | Major | No pressure alarms (PAH/PAL) are defined between normal control and the trips. The operator gets no warning before the flare valve opens or a trip occurs. | Add PAH and PAL with defined operator responses. |
| D10 | 6.2.6 | Major | The relief basis is incomplete: | Add the relief basis and makeup gas, and state that vacuum relief is the last layer of protection. |
| | | | – no statement that the PSV set point equals the design pressure; | |
| | | | – no relief sizing cases (fire, rollover, barometric change, filling displacement, pump recirculation heat, flash, control valve failure); | |
| | | | – no valve redundancy for maintenance (N+1); | |
| | | | – no discharge location; | |
| | | | – nothing ahead of air-admitting vacuum valves. | |
| D11 | 6.2.7 | Major | "Anti-surge by vendor" has no interface definition. Surge control applies only to centrifugal machines; reciprocating BOG compressors need recycle or unloading capacity control instead. The section does not cover: | Define compressor type, the capacity control method and its split with PIC-501, recycle cooling, and the hardwired and soft interface signals. |
| | | | – recycle gas heating (a recycle cooler or desuperheating is needed); | |
| | | | – how the vendor control interacts with PIC-501; | |
| | | | – trip and permissive signals exchanged with the control system and SIS. | |
| D12 | 6.2.1 | Minor | Capacity control method and load sharing or sequencing for K-501A/B are not described. Whether pressure is controlled in gauge or absolute terms is not stated. Gauge control lets BOG rate swing with barometric pressure, while mechanical limits are gauge. | Specify the control method, the step or stepless capacity sequence, and the pressure basis. Typically control on absolute pressure and protect on gauge, to be confirmed. |
| D13 | 6.2 general | Minor | No link to rollover monitoring or filling-mode strategy (top or bottom fill), both of which strongly affect pressure. | Cross-reference the relevant FDS sections. |

---

## Corrected Section

> Values marked **[TBC]** are proposed and must be confirmed against the tank vendor design data, HAZOP/LOPA and the SRS. Tag numbers must be verified against the P&IDs.

### 6.2 Tank Pressure Control and Protection

**6.2.0 Basis**
- Tank design pressure: **290 mbarg [TBC – tank vendor]**. Design vacuum: **–5 mbarg [TBC – tank vendor]**.
- Mechanical limits and protection functions are in gauge pressure. Normal control may use absolute pressure, to reduce barometric-driven BOG swings **[TBC]**.
- Each layer uses independent transmitters:
  - control: PT-501;
  - flare/makeup control: PT-512;
  - SIS: PZT-510A/B/C, voted 2oo3.

**Pressure hierarchy**

| Level | Setpoint (mbarg) | Function |
|---|---|---|
| PSV-5xx | 290 (= design) | Pressure relief to atmosphere at a safe location |
| PAHH (SIF) | 250 [TBC] | Tank overpressure SIF (6.2.4) |
| PIC-512 to flare | 220 [TBC] | Excess BOG to flare via PV-512 |
| PAH | 200 [TBC] | Operator alarm |
| PIC-501 normal | 120 [TBC] | BOG compressor capacity control |
| PAL | 60 [TBC] | Operator alarm |
| PALL (SIF) | 30 [TBC] | Tank underpressure SIF (6.2.5) |
| PIC-515 makeup gas | 20 [TBC] | Vacuum-breaker gas injection |
| VRV-5xx | –5 (= design vacuum) | Vacuum relief (air ingress), last resort |

**6.2.1 Normal pressure control.**
- PIC-501 controls tank pressure at 120 mbarg by adjusting BOG compressor K-501A/B capacity, using **[step unloading / recycle / speed – TBC]**.
- One compressor is duty and one standby. The standby starts automatically when the duty unit is at full capacity and pressure is still rising above **[TBC]**, or when the duty unit trips.
- Below the minimum compressor capacity, the vendor recycle maintains minimum flow. If pressure keeps falling, the low-pressure override in 6.2.3 applies.
- BOG is routed to **[recondenser / fuel gas / send-out – TBC]**. On loss of this outlet the compressors unload or trip on their own protections, and PIC-512 maintains tank pressure via the flare.

**6.2.2 Excess BOG to flare.**
- PIC-512 (PT-512) opens PV-512 to flare when tank pressure exceeds 220 mbarg. It closes PV-512 as pressure returns to normal.
- A low-pressure override closes PV-512 below **80 mbarg [TBC]**, whatever the PIC-512 output.
- PV-512 fail position: **[TBC per HAZOP]**.
- The PAH alarm at 200 mbarg warns the operator before flaring starts.

**6.2.3 Low-pressure control.**
- At PAL (60 mbarg) the operator is alarmed.
- PIC-501 has a low-pressure override that reduces compressor capacity to minimum below **70 mbarg [TBC]**.
- PIC-515 injects makeup gas from **[send-out header / vaporised LNG – TBC]** through PV-515 to hold the tank above 20 mbarg.
- Makeup gas capacity covers the worst credible low-pressure case: maximum send-out with compressors at full capacity plus a barometric pressure rise **[TBC]**.

**6.2.4 Tank overpressure SIF (PAHH, 250 mbarg, 2oo3, SIL [TBC per LOPA]).** On activation the SIS:
- closes tank inlet and filling valves **[tags TBC]** and stops ship or truck unloading;
- stops in-tank pump recirculation to the tank;
- forces PV-512 fully open to flare.

The BOG compressors are **not** tripped by this function and remain available to remove vapour. Compressor self-protection is handled by the package instrumentation (6.2.8). Reset is manual, from the field or a supervisory reset, after pressure has returned below **[TBC]**.

**6.2.5 Tank underpressure SIF (PALL, 30 mbarg, 2oo3, SIL [TBC per LOPA]).** On activation the SIS:
- trips BOG compressors K-501A/B;
- closes PV-512;
- trips the LNG send-out pumps **[TBC]**.

Makeup gas (6.2.3) stays in service. Reset is manual.

**6.2.6 SIF bypass management.**
- SIS bypasses are not available from the operator HMI.
- Maintenance overrides are applied per transmitter through a key-switch or permit-controlled function, under the site bypass procedure. Every override must be:
  - logged;
  - time-limited, with an alarm when the time expires;
  - shown by a persistent HMI alarm.
- While one transmitter is overridden, the function degrades (e.g. 2oo3 to 1oo2) and is not defeated.
- Overrides are not permitted during filling, unloading or cooldown.
- Compensating measures are as defined in the SRS.

**6.2.7 Pressure and vacuum relief.**
- Pressure safety valves PSV-5xx (N+1 installed **[TBC]**) are set at the design pressure of 290 mbarg. They are sized for the governing case among:
  - fire;
  - rollover;
  - barometric pressure fall;
  - filling displacement and flash;
  - pump recirculation heat input;
  - control or SIF failure.
- PSVs discharge to atmosphere at a safe location **[or flare – TBC]**.
- Vacuum relief valves VRV-5xx (N+1 **[TBC]**) are set to protect the –5 mbarg design vacuum. Because they admit air, they are the final layer, below makeup gas and the PALL SIF.

**6.2.8 BOG compressor package protection.**
- K-501A/B are **[reciprocating / centrifugal – TBC]**.
- Machine protection (anti-surge if centrifugal, or recycle/unloading if reciprocating) is provided by the vendor package.
- Recycle gas cooling or desuperheating is provided to keep suction temperature within limits.
- Package protections include low and high suction temperature, high discharge pressure and temperature, motor overload, and suction drum high-high level.
- Interface signals between the package and the control system/SIS (capacity demand from PIC-501, running and trip status, permissives, SIS trip inputs) are defined in the interface schedule **[ref TBC]**.

**6.2.9 Related functions.** Rollover detection and the filling-mode strategy, which affect tank pressure, are covered in sections **[TBC]**.
